items.text: The Journey of Miracles patch is live! Time to jump back in! 🔥
We buffed some Divine Blessings that felt a bit boring, fixed some bugs, made balance adjustments, and added some quality-of-life improvements.

In this patch, we also made Performance Improvements! We believe these changes will have a significant impact on the game's overall performance and help reduce crashes across Steam, consoles, and Android.
We’ve also made the Hell Clock Original Soundtrack available in high quality for those who want to enjoy the music outside the game!
A lot of these changes came directly from our community feedback, so thank you, as always, for helping us make the Hell Clock experience even better!
Optimized lighting and shadows throughout the game.
Improved performance of Skills, Pajeú's visual effects, and enemy effects.
Reduced overall memory usage and memory leaks.
Improved memory management when loading and unloading levels, especially on lower-end devices.
Improved performance across all levels in the game.
Reduced performance spikes and stuttering during gameplay.

Fixed issues with Celestial Jaguar Attack Hitboxes.

items.text: First of all, thank you for your patience over the past months without updates!
Our team has been hard at work putting the finishing touches on Update 2.1, but now our new Major Update is live on Steam, PS5, Xbox Series and Android.
As you may already know, Journeys are Hell Clock's take on the traditional Season/League system. Back in July, we introduced Journey of Nightmares, and now it's Miracle time!

notes.title: The best part? Our Journeys never go away.

items.text: Unlike traditional seasons, each Journey remains permanently available when creating a new save. You can play whichever Journey you want, whenever you want, or even experience them all at once. No FOMO, no missing out on content.

And if you haven't experienced Journey of Nightmares yet, now is the perfect time to jump in! With over 80 new Relics, 12 new biomes, and the Endless Nightmares game mode, there's plenty of content to explore alongside Journey of Miracles!

In Journey of Miracles, you'll encounter Tainted Statues offering powerful rewards to those who fulfill their oath to cleanse a Defiled Sanctum. Accepting the challenge will transport you to a new combat arena featuring fast-paced survival encounters, unpredictable enemy combinations, dangerous new enemy affixes, deadly environmental hazards, and, of course, powerful Divine Blessings and Boons!

items.text: We're thrilled to share a sneak peek of our massive new free update: The Journey of Miracles. If you haven't played Hell Clock since launch, now is the perfect time to jump back in! We've added and improved so much that it completely changes the game.
Here is a quick preview of what awaits you in this new journey:
Defiled Sanctums & Divine Blessings: Find new statues in the dungeons and pledge to cleanse the Defiled Sanctums. If you survive, you'll earn Divine Blessings.
The Underground Crypt: A brand-new area in Act 1 featuring fresh enemies and an unpredictable new mini-boss.

Play at Your Own Pace: In Hell Clock, there is no FOMO! Our journeys are not timed. You can toggle them on or off whenever you start a new save, and even play Journey of Miracles and Journey of Nightmares at the exact same time.
Dozens of new Unique Relics, including two brand-new Relic types, Manifested Miracles and Miracle Droplets, plus 3 new Unique Relics created by members of our community!

But wait, there is more! We're super excited to announce that alongside the new update, we'll also be releasing the official Hell Clock Artbook! Get ready to dive deep into the concept art, character designs, and the dark lore behind our cursed world.
Thank you so much for your continuous support. We hope you enjoy everything coming in this update.
See you in Hell! 🔥
New week, new patch. Let's get into it.

notes.title: Reliquary and Relic Reward Screen Improvements

items.text: As Hell Clock has grown in complexity, the Reliquary has also been expanded far beyond its original design. As a result, even changes to this screen that seem simple may require significant time and careful work to avoid accidentally destroying everything introducing new issues. That's why some of the most requested improvements, such as customizable tabs, aren’t in the game yet.
That said, we’re bringing two small quality-of-life improvements:
Season-exclusive Relics will now display the Season Icon on the Relic tooltip.
The Relic Reward Screen and the Reliquary will now display a highlight icon on Relics you haven’t collected yet.
Relic Fixes
This patch includes several fixes for Relics that were not working properly.
As a result, most of these Relics should feel "stronger", not because they were buffed, but because we've fixed core mechanics that weren't working as intended.
Crimson Necklace: Fixed the Relic converting Physical Damage into Lightning Damage instead of Fire Damage.
Moldy Skull: Fixed an issue where the relic was removing half of the player’s damage instead of applying the effect described in the Affix.

Infested Skull: Fixed the Relic Affix not correctly using (Relic Roll × Shadow Dash Damage) to calculate the explosion damage. Also fixed the Explosion Radius not scaling correctly with Skill Area of Effect modifiers.
The Crossing: Fixed the Affix Roll not correctly affecting the Bleed application interval. We’ve also improved rounding precision for Affix values below 3 for every affix in the game.
Throwing Spear: Fixed the Spear projectile damage not scaling with Projectile Amount and the Affix Roll not being correctly applied as the projectile’s base damage.
Crimson Sword: Fixed the Relic’s Roll being displayed as a multiplicative bonus instead of a multiplicative-additive bonus.

Voice of War: Fixed an issue where the Relic could grant multiple instances of the damage buff when more than one Brute was active at the same time. The damage buff will now also remain active if the Brute dies during the Taunt.
Scout’s Medal: Fixed the Affix not working correctly when combined with other Movement Speed modifiers.

Mother of Perpetual Help (and other Effect Status Areas): There was an issue where Mother of Perpetual Help’s buff was not being correctly reapplied when moving from one Slow Time bubble to another. While investigating this, we discovered a broader problem with how Effect Areas were handled. This fix now applies to all Status Effect Areas.
Other Fixes and Quality of Life Changes
Relaxed Mode’s “Come Back Stronger” popup will now appear only once per run after 7 minutes, instead of appearing after each floor.
Shrine buff effects are now revealed when hovering over a Shrine or when getting close to interact with it using a controller.
Second Wind activation now clears all remaining delayed damage instances (such as Endurance damage over time effects) before resurrecting the player.
Fixed Nina’s Monster hitbox position, allowing Brutes and Charia Summons to consistently land their attacks.
Fixed an issue where breakables would respawn between waves on the Seven O'Clock Train.

Our team remains focused on addressing the most impactful issues, from smaller fixes to larger and more complex problems. We haven’t forgotten about the performance issues and crashes some players are experiencing, both on PC and consoles. Unfortunately, these are among the more challenging issues we’re currently working through.
Whenever possible, we’ll continue to bring improvements that enhance the overall player experience.
That’s all for this update. Thank you once again for your patience and for the incredible support you’ve continued to show us.
Abraços
~ The Hell Clock Team

The release of Cursed War (finally!), our console launch, and the Race Challenge.
2.0 is the biggest update Hell Clock has received to date. Seeing all of you dive into Cursed War new story arc, challenges and Endgame systems has been amazing.
To every member of Hell Clock’s community that helped us with playtesting, feedback and bug hunting (even after Palworld's shadow drop right in our faces) we are grateful for all your support!

As always, launch week also means bugs. Today’s patch focuses primarily on fixing unintended Relic and skill behavior, Campaign and Endgame progression blockers, Localization issues and many other problems you reported over the last few days.
Rumble Support for Gamepads
We've added gamepad rumble feedback to every skill in the game, making combat feel much more responsive when playing on gamepad.
Localization
We fixed some missing or placeholder translations introduced in 2.0, most of them affecting Unique Blessings and Unique Relics.
About the PS5 Version

Some players are experiencing a critical issue causing crashes and save data loss. This issue has only been observed on the PS5 version of the game. Our team is fully focused on resolving them as quickly as possible.
We are also aware that the Ascension mode is currently broken on PS5. This problem has now been fixed, and Ascension will be fixed in the next update.
What we are currently working on?
We're continuing to improve the game's overall performance.
Investigating an issue where players can receive more Constellation Points than intended from Cursed Shrines.
We're also looking into a issue preventing some players from claiming their Twitch Drops,
First of all, thank you to everyone who took part in the Race. Who needs the World Cup when we've got multiple streams open, watching all of you battle for first place?
We'll announce the winners soon! Until then, keep pushing those builds and we'll see you in Hell.

items.text: Greetings, backlanders.
The launch of 1.1 was our smoothest one so far, while at the same time being the game's biggest update ever! This made us happy, but it doesn't mean there isn't stuff to fix!

The main motivation behind this update is adjusting the difficulty of the early endgame, especially for Regular difficulty players. Our testing both internally and on PTR was mostly focused on Veteran difficulty, and we dropped the ball a bit with the difficulty curve coming out of the campaign for novice players.
Early Abyss is now a bit more manageable than in 1.1.0, and hopefully this encourages more players who are new to the ARPG genre to get invested and take their builds to their limits!

We have also found and fixed a couple of nasty bugs with the new Headless Doll Unique. It basically, uh, didn't make much sense, to be honest. It was giving a LOT more Summon Damage than it should in most cases, but sometimes it would give less.

We have NO intention to nerf your builds that you already have going for 1.1, so we are applying a significant buff to Headless Doll that should bring it to about the same power level as it was before this patch, in the best cases. If you are playing Summons, your damage might change a bit (either up or down), but hopefully not more than 15-20%.

This buff, however, is temporary. Headless Doll was capable of performing WAY beyond intended due to these bugs, and this buff is a way to compensate for that and make sure your Summon builds are still performing at the same level for now. But in 1.2 (est. late November) this buff WILL be reverted, so Summons can return to dealing damage more in line with the other archetypes in the game.
We have also noticed some issues with Chinese localization and fixed those! We apologized to your Chinese friends, and hope to do better in the future.

And although we are generally very happy with the current state of Hell Clock's build variety, with basically all skills being strong in endgame and a variety of different builds being able to clear Void, we are giving a few buffs to Bombardment, Spectral Knives and Veil of Quills to get them more in line with the rest of the meta.
Cheers!
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team

Hey backlanders,
Today we want to show the (extensive!) patch notes for our upcoming “Clockmaker’s Tools” update, coming September 29th!
By posting as much information as we can early, we hope we can have a conversation about the changes, and also allow you to prepare ahead of time.

Since this update brings significant overhauls to several systems, items and skills, we thought it would be valuable to also do our very first Design Manifesto explaining our reasoning behind each of these changes.
We believe that transparency and communication (as well as us being humble and changing things when we are wrong) are the key for us to make Hell Clock the best game it can be.
We won’t get into Crafting in this Manifesto, since we already did a deep dive on it last week, which you can read here!
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1782460/view/515221043692962978"]
So without further ado, let’s get into it!

notes.title: Why are we even making changes?

items.text: The game’s been out for a relatively short time, and has done well enough in terms of reviews and sales - so why are we making such sweeping changes to the RPG systems?
We want the game’s defenses to matter, and the challenge of building defensive layers into your builds to be fun and satisfying
We want damage taken and healing to be more of a “battle of attrition”, and less “spiky”
We want Boss fights to never devolve into boring slogs
We want more build variety in the game, with more skills and combinations being viable in both campaign and late endgame
We want our endgame difficulty scaling to be more sensible, and have a stronger foundation for the upcoming Endless Nightmares
We want the Veteran Campaign to be a bit easier, but Abyss and Oblivion to be much harder!

notes.title: What we DON’T WANT to do

items.text: We don’t want to nerf any already existing builds. Any build that is S-tier now should remain S-tier when the patch drops \[Mark’s note: except for Manaloop, and Silver Bullets+Powder Bag. We absolutely had to nerf those two :( ]
We don’t want crafting to add even more power creep to the game
We don’t want Boss fights to resort to cheap one-hit kills
We don’t want S-tier builds to blow through the entire endgame like it’s nothing, leaving you bored and unfulfilled
We don’t want you to alternate between feeling immortal and suddenly getting one-shot.

Hell Clock is currently suffering from a common issue in ARPGs: the defenses start sensible enough, but as the game progresses, you become basically immortal - until something suddenly one-shots you. In our game this is happening mostly due to a couple of outliers. The first one was Lifesteal, which was reworked in 1.0.3; the other one is Conviction.

The issue with Conviction is that it is very weak if used at low values, and game-breakingly strong if invested in. There are currently many methods to get Conviction to the hundreds of thousands with minimal effort, and to millions with a bit more effort.
We are reworking Conviction from the ground up, and here are the major changes:
Conviction is now capped, and the cap starts at 100% of your maximum Mana
All “Conviction Gain” affixes have been replaced with “Max Conviction” bonuses

Conviction Decay is drastically reduced and is no longer linear: it decays fast if you are at or near your Max value, and slows down as the ratio diminishes, becoming very slow if you are in the bottom 25% of it.
Conviction Decay Resistance nodes, affixes and blessings have been slightly reduced across the board, but are still in the game

The major sources of Conviction (“Conviction from Mana”, the “Closed Body” Skill, and the “Holy Water” and “Mother of Perpetual Help” Uniques) have been reduced to be in line with the new Conviction economy
Most effects that would grant you a flat amount of Conviction (such as the “Breath Mask” or “Silver Bullets” Uniques) have been reworked to grant you a percentage of your Max Conviction instead
The UI bar that represents Conviction now makes a lot more sense, being based on your Max Conviction instead of your Life

Our goal with these changes is to stop infinitely-scaling Conviction, but also to make it more consistent at lower values than it currently is. Earning Conviction will be much harder than before, but it will also decay much less, especially at lower values.

We are also bringing Evasion down a notch by reducing most Evasion sources (as it is currently extremely easy to cap Evasion with minimal investment), and also making it not work against Area attacks and ground effects. Basically any ground effects and any attack in the game which has a ground indicator, as well as secondary area effects from attacks (such as the Headcutter's ground slam) are no longer possible to Evade.

notes.title: Less Monster Damage, Less Player Recovery

items.text: The Conviction and Evasion changes, however, are not being made in a vacuum. With both Lifesteal and Conviction brought back in line, we are rebalancing all enemy damage scaling in the game from scratch. Our goal is to make the damage you take less “spiky”, and more of a battle of attrition, so all sources of effective health pool (EHP) recovery have been reduced.
This is effectively a global increase on “time to kill” against players, combining a reduction in monster damage with a reduction on players’ recovery ability.

Our goal is for you to see far less deaths where you are brought from full life down to zero in less than a second, and more often see your death approaching as you run out of options and resources instead.

This brings us to the issue of Boss fights, which are an absolute pain to deal with in ARPGs. The reason for it is the sheer variety of player capabilities that the vast customization of ARPGs allows for: you can have two characters reach the same Boss at the same point in their progression, but one of these builds has 4,000 Life, uncapped Resists, and just a single defensive layer, and can kill the Boss in 50 hits; while the other one can have 10,000 Life, capped Resists, and two or even three layers, but takes 1000 hits to kill the same Boss.

We want to keep our “no one-hit kills” design ethos, and we also want to make sure that building defenses and a “tanky” playstyle is rewarding; but we also need to make sure that builds that have good defensive layers can’t just sit still and facetank every single Boss while dealing basically no damage, for 5 minutes or longer.
With these goals in mind, we are implementing the “Curse” system in all Bosses and Unique enemies. If you are familiar with the Act 3 final Boss, this is the exact same mechanic.

Every Boss attack will inflict a few stacks of Curse on you, with the more impactful and easier to dodge ones contributing far more stacks. Each Curse stack will reduce all of your Resistances, and can even bring them to negative values. Defeating the Boss/Unique monster will instantly remove all Curse stacks.

This will allow us to tune Boss damage in a way in which any appropriately-scaled character is guaranteed to not get one-hit-killed by any mechanic the first time they get hit. As the fight progresses, getting hit again (especially with the most telegraphed attacks) will make everything hurt more and more, with tankier builds of course being able to resist a lot further, but overall the challenge and tension of the Boss being maintained.

As a small indie studio, complex and intricate Boss fights are the single most expensive thing for us to create, so although we recognize that the fights in Hell Clock are much simpler than what you’d see in a AAA game such as Path of Exile 2, we hope that with a few well-placed changes we can have them do their job and provide a satisfying experience that fits our game’s structure.
With survivability out of the way, let’s talk about damage.

Although the current build variety isn’t terrible for a 1.0 release of a new ARPG - and is bound to increase a lot more as we release all of the Constellations, new Relics and new Skills - we believe it’s far from where it should be.
If you consider the current meta, the only types of builds that can currently crush Oblivion easily are using at least one of these 3 techs:
Manaloop (as it completely breaks the game with infinite cast speed);
Scaling damage via extreme stacking of Conviction (either with Silver Bullets or Written Promise);
Stacking ungodly amounts of Projectile%

These three things were at least an order of magnitude above all other options in the game, so bringing them back in line makes everything much saner. It also allows us to reduce enemy Life scaling from Act 2 Normal onwards, which frankly could get a bit silly.

As funny as Manaloop is, it obviously needs to go. We are introducing changes to the Oxumaré Constellation and to Judgement with the goal of disabling looping. Both changes are also positive, since it aligns Oxumaré with its original design goal of reducing larger cooldowns (it was never meant to be a tool to increase cast speed of Spells), and Judgement is also getting more attention (more details on the section below).

We were also worried about how Silver Bullets triggering Powder Bag made for very dull buildcrafting, as it outperformed every way of triggering PB and was by far the less creative or interesting. Silver Bullets are no longer Physical, and now add Lightning damage to your shots. With all Constellations and Relics we have planned, the Silver Bullets + Powderbag combo will be viable again in the future, but it will take a bit more investment than it did in the previous iteration.

Apart from these two particular cases above, our goal is to NOT nerf any build that is already working and doing well in the endgame. If you are running Splitshot with loads of projectiles, clearing screens with Mark of the Vulture, and melting bosses with Summon Rosary, do not worry - our intention is not to nerf anything, we are just reducing the damage ceiling of the game and reducing the enemy scaling along with it.

Hopefully this will pave the way for far more build options being viable, even before the introduction of new content to the game. It will also give us a more solid base to work with for future updates, without losing control over our scaling and ending up with Bosses having literal trillions of Life a few months down the road.

We are also introducing several changes to the Soulstone and item drop economy in general. The current iteration of the Soulstone economy incentivizes players to go back and farm earlier completed Acts instead of going as far as they can on their current Act - especially in Ascension.

Overall, later Acts will always be more rewarding now, with greatly increased drop rates and also with recycle gains from Relics scaling with higher Tiers as well. We are also updating the Campaign drop tables to ensure that Relics from Act 1 can show up as Tier 2 drops when playing Act 2 of the Campaign.

For 1.1 we are also reworking the scaling of the World Tiers. Abyss and Oblivion should be MUCH harder now, as it was originally intended, and will require well-rolled Relics and optimized builds to complete.

We understand that the vertical endgame will never feel fully satisfying until we have Endless Nightmares out, offering a more fleshed out experience. But still, many of you have demonstrated that you are eager to push your builds to the limit and want something right now that will allow you to do that.

So for 1.1 we are also introducing a new, final World Tier: Void. It is designed to be impenetrable to all but the most powerful builds you can come up with, and will yield no Constellation points - its purpose is purely to serve as a temporary pinnacle activity while we work on Endless Nightmares.
Void is ridiculously challenging and completely optional. We do not expect the vast majority of players to be able to clear it.
After Endless Nightmares is released early next year, we will probably remove Void and keep only Abyss and Oblivion in the game.
We have made several other smaller changes that we think need some clarification about our motivations.

We are reducing all crit bonuses available in the game. This is part of our effort to reduce the overall damage scaling in Hell Clock, but it’s also because Crit felt almost mandatory in endgame, especially with how little investment was required to reach the crit cap (100% crit chance). Again, this is not intended as a direct nerf to crit-based builds, as the enemy Life scaling has also been decreased to account for it.

We are bringing some underperforming Skills up a notch, to compete with the more popular ones. This includes buffs to Bombardment, Phantom Marksmen, Summon Brute, Passage, Repeater, Matadeira, Old Bell, and a big buff to the Retaliation damage of Closed Body. This is part of the overall effort to increase build variety and creativity.

Reflexes has been reworked into “Spectral Knives” to provide better QoL as well as more damage. It now works similarly to a Prayer, with its effect always active, and the activation providing a temporary boost to damage, throw speed and knife regen speed. All Spectral Knives Uniques have been revised and buffed. It is also getting strong synergies by having a natively increased Bleed chance and by gaining the “Spell” tag.

Some Unique Relic Blessings have been removed, either to reduce the overall size of Blessings Decks (increasing their consistency over time) or because those effects could get a bit silly (in the case of Northerner’s Belt cooldown reductions, for example).

Judgment has been changed not only to avoid Manalooping, but also to make the Skill more interesting, and its Relics actually useful. The new base cooldown for Judgement makes it less of an “add to any build for free damage” tool, and requires you to make use of its Unique effects to really take advantage of the extremely powerful Resistances debuffs.We’ve also brought its Blessings down a bit, because the insane amounts of Res reduction that could be achieved with Judgement made it auto-include in all builds, which is never a good thing. To compensate for all these nerfs, we are buffing the effectiveness of Judgement for Ailment builds, giving it a more specialized role in the meta (while still being useful for Res reductions for basically any build, just to a lesser degree than previously).
We have also given enormous buffs to two “meme” techs in the game, in the hopes that you will now be able to take them and turn them into hilariously viable builds in patch 1.1.
With the new focus on increasing the “time to kill” on players, all Life draining effects (such as The Sacrificed or Wheel of Death) have been significantly reduced.

Also to keep in line with the new survivability scaling in the game, most sources of Resistances in the game have been reduced, and capping Resistances in higher World Tiers and Hell Levels will now be an actual goal instead of being basically “free”. Higher World Tiers are also reducing Defenses as well as Resistances.

Greetings Backlanders,

We are celebrating one month of Hell Clock's release with our third big patch! This time there aren't that many changes, as we focused on the one thing our community has been most vocal about: performance, performance, performance.

We have worked very hard (seriously, type some "o7" for our coder Murilo) to make a performance patch that would actually matter and improve your experience in a meaningful way. We have also drastically reduced Load times after the initial one.

We have recruited some volunteers from Discord to test it out and ensure that we are actually tackling the most pressing problems affecting some high-end builds. So a round of applause to our community members who volunteered their time in the interest of making the game better for everyone: BaZinga, Fatalaris, hardwii, hiragi, Justlfied, Monddoc, Ownage, tetris19023, Tetsuo9999, TheOlBamboozler.

With all that said, a caveat: this patch is not a magical silver bullet that will resolve 100% of performance issues overnight. This is a significant push, and we have seen massive improvements to some users, while others are reporting improvements limited to the 15-20% range. So your mileage may vary, and we will keep working on it.

We have a couple of OG Steam Decks around here, and the performance on the Decks seems to be drastically improved, with the game never dipping below 30 frames, with the exception of some heavy endgame builds that can bring it down to the 15-20 fps range (instead of freezing the game or bringing it down to the "unplayable" 1-2 fps range, as it was before).

Optimizing performance for PC in 2025 is a nightmare as there's such a staggering diversity of devices and setups out there, each with their own quirks. We will keep working on performance during the following months, so please report (respectfully) any lingering issues you might be still experiencing in the Steam forums, Discord, and social media. We don't always reply, but I assure you we read ALL of those in a group effort between myself, Lucy, Carol and Mason.

notes.title: Lifesteal is dead, long-live Life Leech

items.text: The major gameplay change for patch 1.0.3 is a rework of Lifesteal. Originally this was scheduled for patch 1.1 (which will introduce an overhaul of ALL defenses and the enemy damage scaling), but we've seen way too many cases of rookie players equipping a single Lifesteal ring and becoming almost immortal, to the point of accessing areas they were not supposed to yet, and spending 30-60 seconds hitting on a single white mob. It made our eyes bleed, truly.

We decided to scrap the concept of "turning damage into Life" completely, and have introduced something that makes more sense in the broader systems design of Hell Clock. "Life Leech" is now capped at a percentage of your maximum Life every second, and is not cumulative.

In practical terms, it now functions basically as an extra layer of Life Regen per second, but to activate this layer you need to cause damage (at least once every second). It benefits Life stackers more than any other build, and also benefits builds which take advantage of Life Gain and Regeneration bonuses.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/83c83bd88613cee15a4ccd5c1c404e620ae57a6b.png"]
You've been asking for this since release, and we've listened: we have added a Dummy to Quixeramobim, allowing you to test your Skills, builds and rotations before descending into Hell.

The Dummy is currently very simple. In the future we hope to increment it with more advanced features such as DPS meters, the ability to spawn multiple dummies, and being able to spawn them as Rares, Uniques or Bosses, as well as adding Resistances and other defensive effects to them.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/fd5194f746a992083e6d3d671003f59fc7db4fcd.png"]

Patch 1.0.3 should be our last one before our fist Major one: Update 1.1 - Clockmaker's Tools. We are currently on track to hit our September deadline, and we are aiming to land around the time of the Autumn Sale (Sep 29th).

Besides the exciting addition of Crafting, and the much-requested QoL features of Gear Stash, Search/Filter function and Loadouts, we will also introduce a Defenses rework, and a major rebalance of the entire game to increase build diversity and improve the enemy scaling.
Stay tuned to our socials and Steam blogs in the next few weeks for more information on Clockmaker's Tools!
Cheers,
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team

Hello Backlanders,
Today we celebrate 2 weeks of launch for Hell Clock - and what better way to do that than to release a massive update that addresses some of your most urgent requests?
Today's patch 1.0.2 brings a lot of fixes and changes, but most importantly it adds a new campaign balance and a new Endgame system.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/339b74684ed1f7b40107fc357b25939a3a01bddb.jpg"]

"Regular" difficulty tries to address every single pacing, balancing and difficulty issue raised by our players in the last 14 days, and we think it serves as a great introduction for Hell Clock. Any pre-existing Save files will be considered "Veteran", so if you want to experience this streamlined version of the campaign, you will need to create a fresh new Save file.

Also, when you finish the Campaign, there is no more need for the scary Ascension reset: you can keep all of your progression from the Campaign and take it straight into Abyss and Oblivion - and also collect new item Tiers for your build! While we expect the vast majority of players to be able to clear Abyss, we expect Oblivion to challenge your build and take your character to the limit.
Whenever you want to give the challenge of Ascension a try, it has been moved to its own separate save file, and unlocks when you complete the Campaign once on any difficulty.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/cbc16221a95812f76c7e0405b3b7785f5a9fd206.jpg"]

Also, we understand that testing new builds is currently very cumbersome due to the lack of a Gear stash of some sort. This is a high priority for us right now, and will come in the next update (check the "What's Next" section below for more details), as well as QoL features such as a Search/Filter for your storage and skill trees.

We worked really (REALLY!) hard on bringing 1.0.2 to you as fast as possible, as we recognized a lot of frustration from a part of our community and didn't want them to feel let down. But this is not the last update for Hell Clock - quite the opposite!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/fd5194f746a992083e6d3d671003f59fc7db4fcd.png"]

Our focus is currently on our first Major Update, which we call Clockmaker's Tools (1.1.0), and our current target date for it is September 29th. Expect smaller fixes and patches until then, but no new features or significant additions.

notes.title: Here's our development priority, in order

items.text: 1 - Performance, performance, performance. We want to make the game smoother and more responsive for the majority of players, regardless of how many effects they have flying on the screen at once.
2 - QoL for items and skills, including a Gear Stash, Loadouts, and a Search Filter for the Reliquary and the skill trees.

3- Improving the design of Defenses and the overall damage curve of the game. Right now in the late game it feels like you are either immortal or getting 1-shot, which is a terrible feeling in any ARPG, so we want to fix that.
4 - Adding more Constellations and Relics, focus on enabling new and varied builds.

To the more crafty members of the community: if you want to create tools, build planners, wikis, etc., we have created a GitHub repository where we're exposing a lot of game data, including everything that has to do with Blessings and Skill Trees. In the near future we will also include Drop Tables.

If you have stopped playing the game since launch due to the Campaign pacing and/or the Ascension endgame, we invite you to revisit the game and renew your feedback. We have listened to you, we have made significant changes, and we are willing to make more if that's what the community wants.

Thank you for your incredible support so far! You are making the future of Hell Clock brighter and brighter, and we are looking forward to witnessing just how far we can take this game, and how much better it can be as we keep improving it - together!
Cheers,
~Mark and the Hell Clock team

releases.displayName: Major Update Incoming: Improving Progression and Endgame

items.text: Greetings, Backlanders!
We are celebrating one week of release for Hell Clock, and it’s been an incredible ride so far! You have blown us away with your support, and we couldn’t be more grateful.
Today we’ll talk about the two most important pain-points the community has been reporting: the pacing/balance of the campaign; and the endgame.

If these are not what YOU are interested in, we invite you to check out our “State of the Game” post from last week, as I believe it is very much still representative of all of the issues that we plan to fix in the coming weeks.
So with that out of the way, let’s begin!

As we said in State of the Game, the feedback about the campaign balance caught us a bit off-guard. In hindsight it is pretty obvious, but we got “tunnel vision” in the months leading up to release and ended up with a progression balance aimed to please only die-hard ARPG nerds such as myself, to the detriment of the wider audience.

This is our mistake, and we have learned from it. It is not the fault of the player. Our game should offer a reasonable space for learning the systems, while at the same time being an entertaining experience without hours and hours without meaningful progress.
Ideally, we want to turn all of you into huge Exile-like nerds. So here’s our evil plan to achieve that:

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfwtfF5GoQi79j6zXvkOURzzDdR9HiZB4jwZTUozz-GXGSihQ-XqunsTXBRRPFrGV1fta_yFZSRmkJhiWlSWdWR6eBZcC7_4DXA3bgmh0yYOPV2YCO_rP7ylGLRtK5-dNVJrzzWXg?key=-nh-X5jckImUKx-hvQ4i1w"]

When creating new save files, you will be able to choose between two difficulties: Regular and Veteran. These are fundamental changes to the campaign structure and pacing, so you will not be able to change this after the game has started (similar to Softcore/Hardcore).
To design Regular mode, we went through (almost literally!) ALL of your feedback, watched dozens of gameplay VODs, and I personally spent the entire weekend tweaking it.
This is a MAJOR overhaul of campaign pacing and enemy scaling that we hope will address most - if not all - of your gripes so far.

But what if you enjoyed the game as it is today? Do not worry, the “Veteran” difficulty is basically the current balance, relatively untouched. For technical reasons, any existing save file when this Update releases will be considered a “Veteran” save file. You will need to create new games to experience the new “Regular” mode. The two experiences are way too different for it to be a “toggle”.

Speaking of toggle, “Vengeance Mode” and “Relaxed Mode” will still function exactly the same as they do now. You can combine all of these options in any way you want: do you want to play a Hardcore Regular run with Vengeance Mode and Relaxed Mode turned on? You can do it!
As we said before, this is YOUR game, and the only “right” way to play video games is to have fun.

In the months leading up to release, we’ve played Hell Clock internally with a mostly “ephemeral” playstyle, mostly not hoarding Relics and with a focus on the reset-heavy rogue-like nature of “Ascension”.

After release, we have discovered that the majority of players actually play it much differently: a LOT of you enjoy collecting everything, grinding it out, upgrading all Relics and hunting for those perfect rolls to perfect your builds.

While this also sounds obvious in hindsight (since these are staple things of the ARPG genre) we actually underestimated our own game and thought that people would not be as interested in putting so many hours into Hell Clock’s progression.

At the same time, while Ascension feedback has been very positive for people who actually were onboard with the concept, the majority of players are not even willing to give the game mode a try, and you have told us so loud and clear: you want a more “traditional” endgame, you want to push your builds to the limit, and you don’t want to lose any progress while doing so.

We heard you, and we’re already working hard on it! We were also not THAT naive - we knew we were trying something risky with Ascension, so we were already prepared to move very fast and change things around in case it wasn’t well-received.

notes.title: Ascension is moving to a new Save File

items.text: If you’re particularly observant, you may have noticed something in the previous screenshot: Campaign and Ascension were different things.

When this Update launches, we will separate Ascension completely from your main Save file to avoid any confusion. After you beat Campaign once with any save files (whether it’s Regular or Veteran) you will unlock Ascension mode, but it will be a completely separate experience that will live in its own Save file.
And of course, all of the customization options from the Campaign are still available: you can play Ascension in Regular or Veteran difficulties, HC/SC, Relaxed mode and Vengeance mode.

We are also increasing the max save files in the game from 3 to 6. Any existing save files which contain both Campaign and Ascension progression will be split into two separate ones when the update releases.
We believe this is the right choice for Ascension moving forward.

Speaking as Mark: I am personally very invested in Ascension, and the new Endgame options and Save file separation will allow me to cater this game mode fully towards its audience, which will probably be more niche. This will allow me to do very creative and crazy things with this mode without worrying about alienating the wider audience. Think of this going forward as our own little “Ruthless Mode”, and I personally look forward to building it with you!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/d24e6716022d066fad8568c7cffd5887d84ee50f.png"]

The first new Endgame system we want to introduce is called “Abyss & Oblivion”. If you have played Diablo 2, these will basically be our “Nightmare” and “Hell” modes. If you are unfamiliar with this concept, you can think of it as a “New Game+” and “New Game++”.

Abyss and Oblivion will allow you to venture beyond Act 3, keeping all of your existing progression. While we expect most players to be able to complete Abyss, be warned that Oblivion will test you: only the best builds and most hardened Backlanders will see the end of this journey.

You will gain 4 Constellation points when you enter Abyss for the first time, and you will also find 24 additional Cursed Shrines scattered throughout Abyss and Oblivion, providing you with a total of 38 Constellation Points for your late-endgame builds.
And yes, we will add full Constellation re-spec!

We will also introduce a new Skill Tree called “The Oblivion Bell”. As soon as you enter Abyss for the first time, it will fully replace the regular Bell from the Campaign. The Oblivion Bell will offer much deeper progression and customization options for your endgame adventures.

notes.title: Here’s the breakdown for Abyss and Oblivion

items.text: Abyss
* Bosses and Survival events no longer freeze the Hell Clock
* Bosses have new Mechanics
* Uses endgame Drop Tables
* New Dangerous Affixes added to Elites
* -25% to all Resistances
* New enemy scaling
* +12 total Constellation points via Cursed Shrines
Oblivion
* Even harder enemy scaling, will really test your characters
* -50% to all Resistances
* Elites have one additional Dangerous Affix
* Bosses have an Enrage timer
* +12 total Constellation points via Cursed Shrines

Although Abyss & Oblivion will be fun to play through, they do not represent the full vision of Hell Clock’s new vertical endgame. This is why we can’t leave before giving you this following sneak peek:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/b5e556607eb9f6a3a1cb9a21ce38e5d9b9891ac3.png"]"Quem nunca teve um pesadelo... essa noite vai sonhar com Tiriri..."
Endless Nightmares is a mapping endgame, done in the Hell Clock style.
Cleanse the Nightmares and restore order with the guidance of Exu Tiriri, an Umbanda spiritual entity.
A new image of Exu Tiriri will be added to the hub at Quixeramobim after you beat the Campaign. Interacting with it will let Tiriri guide you through your very own custom Nightmare.

You will take your picks between randomly-generated Shards of Nightmare in a sequence. This will create a new 21-Floor Dungeon, and your decisions have shaped its dangers and rewards. Fully clearing Nightmares will unlock higher tier ones, up to T16 - see how high your build can push!

Endless Nightmares will take advantage of the upcoming endgame-exclusive Biomes and maps we’ll be making for The Cursed War to offer a deeply replayable and customizable experience, with randomly-generated dungeons shaped by your decisions.
We don’t want to spoil this mode too much, as it is still a few months away, so stay tuned for more Endless Nightmares previews in the near future!
This is it for now!

To reiterate: ALL of these changes (except for Endless Nightmares) are coming NEXT WEEK in patch 1.0.2. We can’t give an exact day yet because it will depend on QA testing and debugging, but we are aiming for the beginning of the week rather than the end.

Thank you so much for supporting our game. The main reason why we’ve been able to react so fast is that the majority of your feedback has been very clear, helpful and respectful. It helps a lot when the community tells us exactly what they want, as it fills us with confidence and motivation to make the changes.
Hell Clock is just beginning, and we look forward very much to how we’ll build upon this foundation together over the coming months.
Cheers!
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/e5a08de1b97f9b4e2d0dfd2521cc411003e5aa38.png"] Hey everyone, It's been 48 hours since Hell Clock 1.0 was released, and we are deeply, deeply grateful for the results so far. Your feedback has been very positive, critics have been unanimously praising the game, and it has been the fastest selling game of our careers. Does this mean we get to kick back and enjoy a well-deserved vacation? Quite the opposite! We're more motivated than ever to work and make the game better as fast as possible. We are a very small team but we love this game and are pouring our hearts and souls into it, and we hope that it will show over the coming weeks. We have been trying to read every forum post on Steam and Reddit, every Discord conversation, every review, every video and stream, and trying to figure out how to make this game better for you. Let’s talk about that.
State of the Game

Every major patch in the future will be accompanied by a “State of the Game” blog post such as this one. These will be opportunities for us to check in with the community and see if we are in sync with one another. Are we seeing the same issues? Are we out of touch? You tell us!
Explaining Game Mechanics Better

We have not been doing a perfect job at clearly communicating all of the game mechanics and systems in-game, as we should. Today we have added improved feedback for Relic Upgrades, a new Loading Tips system, and full descriptions in-game for all Ailments and how they work.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/65deebbc752b0dfe28457cd72fae158cf1c76a2d.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/52135bbb2adca0b884870c890cd3fb5da6958513.png"]But there is still more to do. We have in the pipeline an overhaul of the Blessings of Foundation screen (the Gold upgrades mid-run), making it clear how this system works and how you can manipulate it in your favor.

In the future we plan to also communicate Skill synergies (“Global Buffs”) better, and also offer a “Game Help” feature in-game that serves as a “Manual” of sorts and goes over things such as how Multiplicative/Additive bonuses work, and more advanced concepts as well.

In the meantime, you (yes, you!) have taken matters in your own hands and created a community Wiki for Hell Clock! It is not fully fleshed out yet, but there’s already a lot of stuff, including all of the calculations and RPG stats in the game.
Check it out here: https://hellclock.wiki.gg/
Introducing Vengeance Mode

Our release has attracted a larger audience than we expected, and with it came different types of players and different expectations. While the Demo had a majority of players who were build-tinkerers and PoE-nerds like myself and others in the Hell Clock team, the 1.0 launch attracted players from the Action-Roguelike camp, and our game is failing to meet some of their expectations.

Those of you who have been following us since the Beta in December know what our philosophy is: this is YOUR game, the players. Our vision is clear and we will always follow it, but we will not force you to play the game our way. If we can offer more customization, more accessibility options, mod support, anything to make sure you can have fun the way YOU want to, we will. That’s how “Relaxed Mode” was born, for example.

Players who are not fans of the Exile-like genre (yet!) have been disproportionally affected by our game’s opacity in some systems, and the result of that has been that they are grinding through the same areas again and again, and eventually burning out of the game.
Hell Clock is NOT designed to be a grindy game, and it is bad design to punish players who may be new to the genre with no clear feedback as to what is wrong in their builds.

This is why we are introducing Vengeance Mode. Similarly to Relaxed Mode, this can be turned on or off at any point. If you don’t care that much about all the “min/maxing” and just want to experience the combat, progression and lore of Hell Clock without having to stop and grind for hours on end, this mode was designed for you.
In Vengeance Mode, damage dealt is increased while damage taken is reduced. With every failed run, these effects are increased to make your next run even more powerful.

Regardless of being an ARPG player or an Action-Roguelike player, you are now a Hell Clock player - this is YOUR game. Use Vengeance Mode. Don’t use it. Turn it on when you feel like the game is dragging. Turn it off when you feel like you want to dig deeper into the build-crafting. The only correct way to play videogames is to have fun.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/373a0a868a155d533d6a0ed04fabd4040b60e8e0.png"]

As you have been spending more time with Hell Clock, a few key quality of life features have risen to the very top of our lists. Although these are not part of this 1.0.1 patch, they are high priority and will be implemented as soon as possible:
A “Search” function for the Stash and Constellations, filtering and highlighting items based on what you are looking for;
A “Loadout” feature to quickly swap between builds;
Improved “Banish” options to have more control over your Blessing draws;
A “Blessed Gear Stash” to facilitate experimenting with builds;
The ability to Respec your Constellations both in Campaign and in Ascension;
Do you agree with this prioritization? Do you think there’s something more important that should be added before any of these? Please tell us!
State of Ascension Endgame

The game has only been out for 48h and it’s still the middle of the week, so the majority of you haven’t reached Endgame yet, so we are still very much in “observation mode” and listening in to all upcoming feedback.
For those who have already reached Ascension, the feedback has been mostly positive, but we already observed a consensus: Ascension runs are dragging out a little too long.

Next week we plan to experiment with a faster Ascension loop, with 5-run chunks instead of 7-run as it stands right now. Drop rates and rewards will be accelerated, so you should experience the same depth of build progression, but it will take 30% less of your time.

We expect upcoming features such as all Constellations, new Unique Relics, Crafting and the endgame-exclusive Biomes/enemies to go a long way towards improving the replayability and enjoyment of Ascension. But in the meantime, please keep the feedback coming, as we’re sure we can make it much more fun together even before all of the extra content is released.

We are aware of performance issues in late game, particularly with some builds that spawn a lot of projectiles and effects. We are working hard on fixing those as fast as possible, and will have more to share soon.

In the meantime, if you are experiencing these performance issues, we recommend you turn off Damage Numbers, since they are bugged and causing significant frame drops in some cases. Also, turning the “Flashing Effects Intensity” slider all the way down can help as well.
Hopefully some of you who are experiencing these issues can gain enough frames by taking these measures to have fun until we are able to fully resolve the problem. We thank you for your patience.
We are also aware of issues with Loading times. We have already fixed one of them, but there is more work to be done and we hope to have more fixes up soon.

For those playing on Steam Deck, some text can be uncomfortably small. This is harder to fix than it seems, as some screens will need a code re-work to allow for text scaling. We don’t have a date estimate yet, but this issue will be fixed.
Update 1.0.1 Patch Notes
Gameplay
New Feature: Vengeance Mode
You can toggle Vengeance Mode ON/OFF at any point;
Vengeance mode increases damage dealt and reduces damage taken when activated;
Every failed run increases the effect of Vengeance, making Pajeú more powerful;
Turning Vengeance Mode off will “save” the accumulated bonuses for when you activate it again, but you won’t accumulate more bonuses if you fail a run with the mode turned off;

We have limited the amount of Summons and Projectiles that enemies can conjure at one time.

Red Portals now provide Shrine Boons of XP and Gold gain for 30 seconds after you enter them. This is a direct buff for Reds and should help with the feeling of "missing out" when you skip some lower floors;

A lot of players did not realize they could actually Upgrade their Relics! We have created a new Onboarding tutorial that teaches you how to Upgrade Relics. We will continue improving this UI in the future;
Bug Fixes
Fixed an issue where the game time would be slowed down after death, requiring the game to be restarted (shout out to DatModz who we were watching live as this happened, lol)
Fixed an issue where endgame Ailment Damage rings were showing a bonus number 10 times higher than they should;

Thanks for supporting our game. Hell Clock is very personal to us, and seeing people from all around the world enjoying something so deeply tied to our history and our culture means a lot to us as Brazilian artists.

It’s been a long and hard road to make 1.0. We’ve been through a lot together over the last few years, and, to be honest, we almost didn’t make it. But we did, and things are looking great right now, and we are grateful.
The fight continues!
Cheers,
~Mark

releases.displayName: Demo Update – Major Improvements, Gamepad Support & New Systems!

items.text: Hey Clockmakers,

Releasing our first Playtest last year was an amazing experience! We were honestly surprised that, even though bad luck had us revealing our ARPG a mere DAY before the biggest ARPG launch of recent memory, we still got a LOT of interest in our game, and a lot of useful feedback.
For this new Demo, we've made significant changes to several systems. Our goal is to improve the early game experience and lay the foundation for the endgame systems that are in development.

We also focused on the main area of feedback from December: controls. We have polished the WASD-movement experience, and properly implemented gamepad support. The gamepad support is still not 100% final quality, so please let us know if you encounter any difficulties or frustrations.
Your Feedback: WASD control scheme had inconsistencies and quality of life issues. Also, Gamepad control was placeholder and did not work on menu screens.

Our Solution: We replaced our "band-aid" control scheme with a polished version. We also officially implemented gamepad support, and everything should be working fine and dandy now (with the exception of the Reliquary screen, which is usable but is still a work-in-progress - it also needs quite a bit of polish for mouse/keyboard as well).
Your Feedback: Clock always ticking down can feel oppressive/unrewarding.
Our Solution: We introduced a new in-game drop that adds more Time to the current run’s clock. You are also guaranteed to get +90 seconds from the main Bosses of each Act.

notes.title: Better Item Pickup and Loot Behavior

items.text: Your Feedback: Sometimes it was annoying to pick up items as a melee build or when blasting quickly through the level. Also, chests took too long to drop their loot and it felt like a waste of precious clock seconds.

Our Solution: We made adjustments to how item drops behave: when you open chests, all items will automatically be attracted to you after they finish dropping (you don’t need to stand next to the chest). Now, this logic also applies to loot from enemies: if you are near the enemy when it dies, the loot will automatically be attracted to you. The only case where loot will stay on the floor is if you kill enemies from a range and never get close.
Your Feedback: The game rewards/incentivizes you for including just a few Skills on your bar.

Our Solution: We introduced a new "Skill Synergies" system which provides passive benefits for ranking up any skill; we have also made the Blessings Deck smaller, and you now have less level-ups per run overall - which means you’ll run out of upgrades sooner if you take only a few skills. ​

Designer Note: It's still a viable option to take only a few Skills if you don’t plan to do deeper than 7-9 Floors in a given run - but now it’s a viable choice instead of always being the optimal play.
Your Feedback: Picking up a "Common" level-up Blessing felt bad.

Our Solution: Our new Blessings balance "squashed" stats and made every upgrade more meaningful; Common and Magic Blessings are now more powerful across the board, and the gap to Rares and Uniques is now less jarring.

notes.title: Smoother Game Flow with Fewer Level-Up Interruptions

items.text: Your Feedback: Too many level-ups interrupted the flow of the game, especially in deeper floors.

Our Solution: We made a new XP Curve with drastically less level-ups per run, especially at the high-end. Our new Blessings balance also means each level up is more meaningful than before, so you still feel that power surge, just with less interruptions.

notes.title: Balanced Gold Costs and Upgrade Depth

items.text: Your Feedback: Gold costs for upgrades sometimes were too expensive / felt random. They also felt a bit shallow/simplistic.

Our Solution: We introduced a completely new "Blessings of Foundation" system, which gives consistent and player-controlling price scaling, as well as raised the skill ceiling of the game from the very first run. This is a complicated feature to explain briefly, so check our in-depth explanation below if you’re interested!

notes.title: New Skill Levels and Mana Rework

items.text: Your Feedback: Mana quickly becomes meaningless and overall doesn’t feel good.

Our Solution: We have introduced a new "Skill Level" system. You can unlock new Skill Levels at the Great Bell, which gives you the choice to use more powerful versions of Skills - but at higher Mana costs.
Designer Note: This system has PLACEHOLDER UI and will be clunky and weird to use in this Demo, we apologize for that, but we wanted to push this out as soon as possible even in this crude state.
Your Feedback: Unique Relics are really cool but there could be more of them early on.

Our Solution: Just for the Demo, we have unlocked all of the Act 1 Unique Relics on the drop pool. This might make your first runs a bit more RNG-heavy than intended, but provide much more choice and exciting build opportunities.

For the final game, we are currently planning to stick to limiting Unique Relic drop pools early on, and increase it as you progress (this is intended to guide newer players so they are not overwhelmed with choice and/or frustrated with bad RNG). But rest assured that the endgame “Hell Mode” will have a huge Relic drop pool. We plan to ship the game with over 100 Uniques, and keep adding more post-launch based on your feedback.
Also, we've finished fleshing out our Ailments system (which was not a "Feedback" reported by you, but it's still a significant improvement! pats own back).
We have replaced the old Gold Totem upgrades with a new tiered system with different categories.

All upgrades and prices start the run at the lowest level, so you won’t see super-expensive stuff right away. By purchasing a Blessing, you will unlock one or more possible upgrades in the same category, so you are in control of how expensive your new Totems will be.

notes.title: There are six Blessings of Foundation categories

items.text: Precision: upgrades related to Critical Chance, Critical Damage and Projectiles.
Force: upgrades related to Elemental Damage, Elemental Ailments and Area of Effect.
Constitution: upgrades related to Life, Life Regen, Endurance and Healing.
Lethality: upgrades related to Physical damage, Melee and Bleed.
Spirit: upgrades related to Mana, Cooldown Reduction, Mana Shield and Conviction.
Alacrity: upgrades related to Move Speed, Attack Speed and Evasion.
